note: Fixes that were tried and measured on a repository, shown in the Solution box next to the ones the report finds itself. Numbers come from the evidence linked with each fix.

fixes.title: Remove the fixed waits from the pghoard test suite
fixes.problem: Every test that starts pghoard waited up to 5 s at shutdown for the upload progress tracker to finish a sleep. The first backup on each test server waited about 45 s for a paced checkpoint, and two timing tests slept longer than they needed to.
fix: Let the upload progress tracker wait on an Event that stop() sets, instead of time.sleep(5). It still checks every 5 s while running.
Run CHECKPOINT in the test database fixture after loading its data, so pg_basebackup's spread checkpoint has nothing to write.
test_handle_site: use a 5 s floor for the backup interval instead of 10 s; it is still far above a backup's 2 s.
Restore stall tests: start the stale limit at 1 s instead of 2 s; the retries tested are the same.
fixes.gain: 36% less test time with every test still running on every version.
fixes.tradeoff: No coverage is lost. The tracker change touches production code, but only how fast it stops; while running it behaves as before.

fixes.title: Run the pghoard tests in parallel
fixes.problem: pytest-xdist is already a dev dependency, but CI runs the suite on one CPU. Each of the three test jobs takes about 52 minutes.
fix: Run pytest with -n auto (one worker per CPU) and pin pytest-xdist 3.8.0 and execnet 2.1.1, so tests run in the main thread where pghoard's SIGHUP handler works.
Give each worker its own port range and its own progress file, so workers never share a port or a file.
Allow 10 WAL senders on the test servers, so a test never waits for the previous test's sender to be freed.
Mark the walreceiver tests serial and run them in a second pytest pass without xdist until their flakiness is understood.
Fail hung tests and jobs: --timeout=900 per test, timeout-minutes: 60 per job.
fixes.snippet:
- run: python -m pytest -n auto -m 'not serial' --timeout=900 test/
- run: python -m pytest -m serial --timeout=900 test/
fixes.gain: Pull request checks in minutes instead of most of an hour.
fixes.tradeoff: More test isolation code. One flaky walreceiver test runs in a slower serial pass. Work-stealing distribution was tried and reverted because some tests depend on the order they run in.

fixes.title: Test each Python and each PostgreSQL version once, not every pair
fixes.problem: Every push runs the PostgreSQL tests for 7 server versions inside each of 3 Python jobs: 21 PostgreSQL suites per push. Most pairs repeat what another pair already checked.
fix: Run the whole suite on each Python version against PostgreSQL 18.
Run each other PostgreSQL version only for the tests that depend on it (mark them needs_pg in conftest and select with -m needs_pg), on one Python version.
Keep the full Python × PostgreSQL matrix in a scheduled weekly run.
Agree the change with the maintainers before merging.
fixes.gain: The biggest single cut in CI time; each job installs only the PostgreSQL it tests.
fixes.tradeoff: Less coverage per pull request: a bug that shows only on one Python × PostgreSQL pair is found by the weekly run, not on the pull request. That is a team decision, so it goes in its own pull request.

result.label: jobs per push; not timed on its own

fixes.title: Stop the WAL receiver without waiting out its keepalive
fixes.problem: With no replication data flowing, the WAL receiver waits up to 10 s in select(), so stopping it took up to 10 s.
fix: Add a socket pair to the same select() and write to it when running is set to False, so the loop wakes at once.
On waking it does what the timeout did (send feedback, ship the unfinished segment), so what is uploaded on stop does not change.
Close the wake-up sockets even when connecting fails.
fixes.gain: Faster shutdown in production and in tests.
fixes.tradeoff: The most complex change of the set, in production code. Worth its own pull request after the others.
